name: Basilica Shrine of Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal
history: The Vincentians (Congregation of the Mission) built the Chapel of the Immaculate Conception at St. Vincent's Seminary in Germantown; the cornerstone was laid in 1875 and it was completed in 1879, opened to the neighborhood at the archbishop's request. In 1927 Fr. Joseph Skelly, CM, created Mary's Central Shrine within it, dedicated on 8 September 1927. It became a basilica in 2022.
arch: A massive granite Romanesque Revival church: a rose window above three doors, two turrets flanking the entrance, and a 125-foot bell tower behind, crowned by a 14-foot bronze statue of Mary.
features: The bell tower holds 23 carillon bells, played by keyboard since 1901.
The Miraculous Medal Perpetual Novena has been prayed here every Monday for almost 100 years.

look.d: A 14-foot bronze statue of Mary stands atop the 125-foot tower.
The rose window glows above the three doorways.
23 bells, played from a keyboard since 1901.

fun: Its Madonna Art Museum holds over 250 works of Marian art from around the world.
journal: Granite and bells in Germantown. Mary on the tower, a novena every Monday.
